newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - German Henkel steps up offer for Loctite.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - German Henkel steps up offer for Loctite.

text.p: German consumer products group Henkel KGaA said on Wednesday it was increasing its offer for the 65 percent stake it does not already own in United States adhesives-maker Loctite Corp to $57.75 per share.

The offer increase, which values the whole of Loctite at $1.2 billion, was widely expected after Henkel's announcement last week that it had made an offer to the Loctite board "at a price in the area of $56" (per share).
Loctite shares closed on Wall Street at $57-7/8 on Tuesday, marginally above the new offer price and a level suggesting that the U.S. market was still hopeful of a yet higher bid.
U.S. analysts last week said a final offer of $60 could not be ruled out.

Henkel's board said in a statement on Wednesday it was still seeking to hold discussions with Loctite aimed at securing a friendly takeover of the company. No such agreement has been reached in talks held thus far.

Henkel's new offer, which is open until January 6 next year, is only valid if acceptances allow Henkel to increase its existing 35 percent stake past the 50 percent threshold that would give it control in Loctite.
Shares in Henkel traded 1.50 marks higher at 70.80 in an overall stronger Frankfurt bourse after the announcement.

German share analysts applauded the deal as reinforcing Henkel's leadership in the world market for industrial and commercial adhesives, but there was some concern about the impact it would have on Henkel's debt.
Such a deal would double Henkel's current debt levels, a fact which contributed to credit rating agency S&P's move to put the company on "CreditWatch" with negative implications last week.
Henkel has nonetheless said it plans to use debt to finance the planned acquisition to avoid having to make a rights issue.

Chemical sector analysts have also noted that Loctite earnings growth in the last four years has not been strong and that Loctite has not appeared to benefit greatly from the growth in demand for adhesives seen this year.
